findings.title: SAML role claim is directly trusted for privileged local role assignment
findings.trust_boundary: IdP assertion claims -> internal RBAC role assignment
findings.iso_42001: Clause 8.2 operational controls for AI system security
findings.pci_dss: Req.7 Restrict access to system components and cardholder data
findings.impact: A user can be provisioned with elevated roles (including super_admin) based on assertion role claims, enabling unauthorized admin access.
reproduction_steps: Observe `roleHint` extraction from assertion attributes in `control-plane/src/modules/auth/saml/handlers.ts:55`.
Observe `roleHint` passed into provisioning at `control-plane/src/modules/auth/saml/handlers.ts:110`.
Observe accepted role allowlist includes privileged roles and is applied directly for new users at `control-plane/src/modules/auth/service.ts:446`.
findings.proof: Code path from SAML assertion -> `roleHint` -> user creation role assignment exists with no server-side mapping policy gate.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace direct role-claim trust with explicit server-managed mapping (IdP group/claim to allowed role table), default-deny unknown mappings, and hard-guard privileged roles behind explicit admin-managed assignment.

findings.title: Session token is transported in URL query parameter during SAML callback handoff
findings.trust_boundary: control-plane auth bootstrap -> browser URL surface -> dashboard callback
findings.pci_dss: Req.4 Protect cardholder data with strong cryptography during transmission
findings.impact: Session token leakage through logs, browser history, intermediary telemetry, and referrer channels can result in account/session hijacking.
reproduction_steps: See token appended to callback URL in `control-plane/src/modules/auth/saml/handlers.ts:122`.
See callback route expects query token in `dashboard/src/app/api/auth/saml-callback/route.ts:16`.
Confirm token used directly as bearer in callback validation at `dashboard/src/app/api/auth/saml-callback/route.ts:27`.
findings.proof: Credential material is moved in GET query string and consumed as active session token.
findings.recommended_fix: Use one-time authorization code exchange (short-lived nonce + server-side lookup) or encrypted POST body handoff; prohibit session bearer tokens in URL components.

findings.title: Logout does not invalidate server-side sessions
findings.component: dashboard auth API + control-plane session validation
findings.trust_boundary: browser logout action -> server-side session lifecycle
findings.pci_dss: Req.8 Identify users and authenticate access
findings.impact: Stolen session tokens remain valid after user logout and can be replayed until expiration.
reproduction_steps: Create test user/session in Postgres (see runtime log).
Call `GET /api/v1/auth/me` with the token: returns 200.
Call `POST /api/auth/logout`: cookie cleared.
Call `GET /api/v1/auth/me` with same token: still returns 200.
findings.proof: Runtime evidence captured in `security-review/RUNTIME_VALIDATION.md` shows token validity unchanged after logout.
findings.recommended_fix: Add server-side logout endpoint to revoke/delete session token record; call it from dashboard logout route before clearing cookie.

findings.title: Policy distribution snapshot ignores org/dept/team scope and trusts client-supplied scope context
findings.trust_boundary: kernel identity and scope claims -> policy data stream
findings.iso_42001: Clause 8.2 operational access controls for AI policy artifacts
findings.pci_dss: Req.7 Restrict access by business need-to-know
findings.impact: A gRPC client can receive policy artifacts outside its intended org/department/team boundary if server-side scope is not enforced.
reproduction_steps: Observe `_orgId`, `_deptId`, `_teamId` parameters unused in `buildFullSnapshot` at lines 61-66.
Observe full active policy query with no org/dept/team filter at lines 75-100.
Observe Subscribe uses client-provided org/dept/team values directly at lines 163-168.
findings.proof: Server-side policy snapshot construction does not apply tenant filters while accepting scope hints from request payload.
findings.recommended_fix: Bind kernel to server-side identity (certificate or registration), reject mismatched scope claims, and filter snapshot query by resolved scope.
findings.diff_snippet:
- export async function buildFullSnapshot(db, _orgId, _deptId, _teamId)
+ export async function buildFullSnapshot(db, orgId, deptId, teamId)
+ // apply org/dept/team WHERE predicates from authenticated kernel identity

findings.title: gRPC distribution can downgrade to insecure transport when MTLS is disabled or unset
findings.impact: If deployed with `MTLS_ENABLED` not set to `true`, policy traffic can traverse without TLS/authenticated peer validation.
reproduction_steps: Read transport toggle at `control-plane/src/modules/distribution/server.ts:280`.
Read insecure fallback at `control-plane/src/modules/distribution/server.ts:306` (`createInsecure`).
findings.proof: Code explicitly supports insecure credentials in non-mTLS mode.
findings.recommended_fix: Fail hard in production profile when mTLS is disabled; require explicit dev profile override with startup guardrail warnings.
findings.risk_acceptance: Acceptable only for isolated local development with documented exception.

findings.title: Session tokens are stored and matched in plaintext at rest
findings.pci_dss: Req.3 Protect stored account data (applied by analogy to auth secrets)
findings.impact: Database read access yields directly reusable session tokens.
reproduction_steps: Observe plaintext token column in schema at `control-plane/src/db/schema/auth.ts:89`.
Observe direct equality match in auth lookup at `control-plane/src/modules/auth/service.ts:362`.
findings.proof: No hashing or keyed derivation is applied to session token values before persistence/lookup.
findings.recommended_fix: Store only hashed session token digests (e.g., SHA-256 with random token value retained client-side), compare digests on lookup, and rotate on privilege events.
findings.diff_snippet:
- token: varchar("token", { length: 128 }).notNull().unique(),
+ tokenHash: varchar("token_hash", { length: 64 }).notNull().unique(),
- eq(sessions.token, token)
+ eq(sessions.tokenHash, sha256(token))

findings.title: Deployment templates include insecure default credentials that can be promoted accidentally
findings.hipaa: 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D) Information system activity review and safeguards
findings.pci_dss: Req.2 Do not use vendor-supplied defaults
findings.impact: If sample values are promoted into non-dev environments, infrastructure and data stores are exposed to trivial compromise.
reproduction_steps: See default credentials in `env.example:18`, `env.example:34`, `env.example:38`.
See fallback defaults in compose at `docker-compose.yml:17`, `docker-compose.yml:49`, `docker-compose.yml:171`.
findings.proof: Templates contain deterministic secret defaults and fallback expansions.
findings.recommended_fix: Remove insecure defaults, require explicit secret injection, and enforce startup refusal when placeholder/default values are detected.
findings.risk_acceptance: May be accepted for isolated local demo only if never reused outside localhost sandbox.

findings.title: Dependency advisory triage shows unresolved vulnerabilities in control-plane and dashboard dependency trees
findings.iso_42001: Clause 8.2 supplier and software lifecycle security controls
findings.gdpr: N/A - indirect technical control, no direct legal article breach without exploitation
findings.hipaa: N/A - indirect control unless vulnerable path is in production runtime
findings.pci_dss: Req.6 develop and maintain secure systems and software
findings.impact: Known vulnerable packages increase exploitability in development/build contexts and can leak into production images if not constrained.
reproduction_steps: Run `bun audit` in `control-plane` (esbuild advisory).
Run `bun audit` in `dashboard` (5 advisories via `shadcn` dependency tree).
findings.recommended_fix: Pin/remediate vulnerable versions, isolate CLI-only toolchains from production image layers, and gate CI on advisory policy.
findings.diff_snippet:
+ bun update
+ bun why <vulnerable-package>
+ remove or isolate non-runtime CLI deps from production artifacts
findings.risk_acceptance: Temporary acceptance possible for dev-only dependencies with documented production exclusion controls.

findings.title: Missing baseline security headers and framework fingerprint exposure on dashboard responses
findings.impact: Reduced browser-side hardening and unnecessary technology disclosure (`X-Powered-By`).
reproduction_steps: Observe no custom headers policy in `dashboard/next.config.ts:3`-`5`.
Runtime `GET /login` response includes `X-Powered-By: Next.js` and no CSP/HSTS in current local setup.
findings.proof: HTTP response capture included in runtime validation log.
findings.recommended_fix: Add strict security headers policy (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy), disable framework signature headers where possible.
findings.diff_snippet:
+ async headers() { return [{ source: '/(.*)', headers: [{ key: 'Content-Security-Policy', value: "default-src 'self'" }, ...] }] }
+ poweredByHeader: false
findings.risk_acceptance: Acceptable only behind a trusted upstream reverse proxy enforcing equivalent headers.

findings.title: Unhandled error logging may leak internals and currently maps some not-found errors to generic 500 responses
findings.entry_point: all REST routes via Elysia onError
findings.trust_boundary: internal exception state -> logs and client response mapping
owasp_top10_2025: A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
findings.iso_42001: Clause 9 monitoring and incident-response evidence quality
findings.impact: Stack/internal error object data can reach logs; operationally, not-found conditions may be misclassified as 500 reducing monitoring signal quality.
reproduction_steps: Review global handler in `control-plane/src/index.ts:52`-`87`.
Observe raw unhandled logging at line 79.
Runtime hit `/api/v1/auth/saml/sso` without SAML metadata and observe 500 + unhandled NOT_FOUND in logs.
findings.proof: Runtime control-plane logs captured in review session show unhandled NOT_FOUND logged and surfaced as INTERNAL_ERROR.
findings.recommended_fix: Normalize Elysia error mapping for known status fields, sanitize log payloads, and avoid logging full raw error objects for auth-sensitive paths.
findings.risk_acceptance: Low-risk temporary acceptance possible if logs are tightly access-controlled and short retention is enforced.

findings.title: Audit aggregate stats endpoints return unscoped cross-department data
findings.trust_boundary: authenticated department-scoped user -> global aggregate analytics
findings.iso_42001: Clause 8.2 access segregation and least-privilege controls
findings.gdpr: Art.32 Security of processing (data minimization and segregation)
findings.pci_dss: Req.7 Restrict access by business need-to-know
findings.impact: Department-scoped users can retrieve tenant-wide aggregate telemetry that may reveal other departments' volume and activity patterns.
reproduction_steps: Inspect `control-plane/src/modules/audit/index.ts:158` and `:177`; handlers call service methods without passing `ctx.user.departmentIds`.
Inspect `control-plane/src/modules/audit/service.ts:110` and `:117`; methods query ClickHouse without department scope filtering.
Comments in module mark this as deferred scoping, confirming known gap.
findings.proof: Role check exists, but object/tenant scoping is not applied to two aggregate endpoints.
findings.recommended_fix: Apply department scope to aggregate queries by passing `ctx.user.departmentIds` into service methods and enforcing scoped WHERE clauses in analytics queries.

findings.title: Control-plane and dashboard containers run as root with writable root filesystem
findings.trust_boundary: container process compromise -> host/runtime impact surface
findings.iso_42001: Clause 8.2 secure deployment and runtime hardening controls
findings.gdpr: N/A - infrastructure hardening control, indirect legal impact
findings.hipaa: N/A - infrastructure hardening control, indirect legal impact
findings.impact: A single RCE in app processes has a larger blast radius when running as root with default capabilities and writable rootfs.
reproduction_steps: Inspect `docker/control-plane/Dockerfile` and `docker/dashboard/Dockerfile`; no `USER` directive is set in runtime stage.
Run `docker inspect` on running services: `interdict-control-plane-1` and `interdict-dashboard-1` show `user=` and `readonly=false`.
Inspect compose service definitions: no capability drop or read-only root filesystem is configured.
findings.proof: Live container inspection confirms root execution and writable rootfs for control-plane/dashboard containers.
findings.recommended_fix: Run runtime containers as non-root, set `read_only: true`, drop Linux capabilities, and mount only required writable paths.
findings.diff_snippet:
# Dockerfile
+ RUN useradd -r -u 10001 interdict
+ USER interdict

# docker-compose.yml
+ read_only: true
+ cap_drop:
+   - ALL
findings.risk_acceptance: May be temporarily accepted only in isolated developer environments with no untrusted network exposure.

findings.title: CI pipeline lacks artifact signing and provenance attestation checks
findings.iso_42001: Clause 8.2 supplier and lifecycle security controls
findings.impact: Build integrity assurance is weaker without signed artifacts and provenance attestations, increasing risk of tampered build outputs being trusted.
reproduction_steps: Inspect `.github/workflows/ci-quality-security.yml`; workflow runs tests/audit/Trivy but does not sign artifacts.
No provenance generation/verification steps (e.g., Sigstore cosign attestations, SLSA provenance) are present in repository workflow config.
findings.proof: Pipeline includes quality and vulnerability scans but no artifact signature/provenance generation or verification stage.
findings.recommended_fix: Add artifact signing and provenance attestation in CI (e.g., cosign keyless signing + SLSA provenance), and verify signatures before deployment.
findings.diff_snippet:
+ - name: Generate provenance
+   uses: slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator/actions/generator@v2
+ - name: Sign image
+   run: cosign sign --yes ${IMAGE_DIGEST}
findings.risk_acceptance: May be accepted temporarily for non-production environments with strict deployment isolation.
